ruleName: Actions That Improve Conditions Affecting the Stroke
title: Can You Break a Branch to Make Your Swing Easier?
question: Your ball comes to rest under a tree. A low branch is blocking your backswing, so you snap the branch off before playing your shot. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: There is no penalty because the branch was only a small twig.
There is no penalty because the branch was dead.
You receive the general penalty because you improved the conditions affecting your stroke.

explanation: A player must not deliberately improve the conditions affecting their stroke by moving, bending or breaking a growing or attached natural object. Breaking a branch to create room for your swing is a breach of Rule 8.1a. If the branch had already been detached from the tree, it would be a loose impediment and could normally be removed.

juniorVersion.title: Can You Snap a Tree Branch to Make Hitting the Ball Easier?
juniorVersion.question: Your golf ball stops under a tree. A low branch is in the way of your backswing, so you break the branch off before you hit your shot. What is the correct thing to do?

choices.text: No penalty because the branch was just a small stick.
No penalty because the branch was already dead.
You get the normal penalty because you made it easier for yourself to hit the ball.

juniorVersion.explanation: You are not allowed to break, bend, or move things like branches or grass to make your shot easier. If you break off a branch that is still attached to the tree so your swing is easier, you get the normal penalty. But if the branch was already on the ground, you could move it.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The first part of your swing when you bring your club back before hitting the ball.
Something added to your score because you broke a rule.
Still connected, like a branch that is still growing on the tree.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind juniors that they must play the course as they find it. Don’t break or bend branches to get a better shot.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may think they can break small or dead branches without any penalty.
Kids might think it's okay as long as it makes the swing easier.
